name: Mississippi River Floodplain
place: St. Louis region, Missouri and Illinois
blurb: Eagles, pelicans and paddlefish on the river beside St. Louis.

tip.title: Try the invasive silver carp
tip.text: Silver carp filter the same plankton that shad, paddlefish and mussels need. Raise them by 100% and see who loses out.

notes: Feeding links were checked against the sources listed where they state them. Where the sources are silent, links come from general ecological knowledge and are illustrative. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.name: River phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae that start the river's food chain. They feed zooplankton, mussels and filter-feeding fish.

A diving duck that migrates along the Mississippi Flyway. It eats tubers, buds, seeds, snails and insect larvae, favoring wild celery. The FWS says the upper river supports up to half the world's canvasbacks.
Eats seeds from moist-soil plants and other plant foods in flooded fields and backwaters.
Lives along banks and marshes, eating aquatic plants.
Browses young trees and shrubs on the floodplain. Coyotes take fawns, and eagles scavenge carcasses.
Cuts cottonwood and willow for food and dams.

nodes.name: River otter
nodes.desc: Hunts fish along the banks. The NPS notes its return since the 1980s as a sign of better water quality.
Dives for fish. The NPS notes cormorants depend on fish.
Scoops up fish from shallows. Breeds on lakes across interior North America and winters on the Gulf coast, and also follows the Mississippi River in winter.
Dives for fish. The NPS notes ospreys depend on fish.
The FWS counts more than 200 nesting pairs in the refuge and nearby public lands. Eats fish and waterfowl and scavenges carcasses.
Lives along the banks, taking fawns, ducks and muskrats. The NPS lists it as a bank dweller.
Powers phytoplankton and the plants of the floodplain.

nodes.name: Bacteria & fungi
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, dead fish and plants and return nutrients to the water and soil.

imgwiki: Upper Mississippi River National Wildlife and Fish Refuge
story: The Mississippi River Floodplain is located in the St. Louis region, across Missouri and Illinois. It features lakes and wetlands along the river corridor. Wildlife found here include the canvasback duck, white-tailed deer, and muskrat.
matters: The area is an important element of the Mississippi Flyway, which is a bird migration route used by about 40% of all North American migrating waterfowl and shorebirds.
